program.name: SGL-001 development program
program.current_formulation_hypothesis: Intranasal mesenchymal-stromal-cell-derived small-EV preparation with defined identity, purity, dose, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay; therapeutic cargo remains to be selected.
program.largest_unresolved_risk: Intranasal CNS exposure observed in rodents may not translate to larger species or humans.
program.next_proposed_action: Run a formulation-controlled biodistribution and pharmacology study with label controls, quantitative tissue exposure, and predefined acceptance criteria, then select a cognition/aging model aligned with the program intent.

claims.statement: Intranasally administered EV preparations have been reported to reach CNS compartments or CNS-resident cells in multiple mouse studies.
claims.rationale: The cited mouse studies reported brain or hippocampal localization after intranasal administration; this does not establish delivery in humans.

claims.statement: Intranasal EV treatment was associated with improved inflammatory, histologic, or functional outcomes in several rodent CNS injury or disease models.
claims.rationale: This is convergent preclinical evidence across distinct rodent models, not evidence of established human efficacy or of efficacy for an as-yet-undefined SGL-001 product.

claims.statement: A clonal immortalized MSC source produced EVs with activity comparable to primary MSC-EVs in one neonatal mouse hypoxic-ischemic injury study, suggesting a testable route to reduce source heterogeneity during scale-up.
claims.rationale: The result supports investigation of a consistent source-cell strategy but does not establish a clinically acceptable manufacturing process.

claims.statement: EV development requires controlled production, separation, identity and purity characterization, functional testing, and transparent reporting because EV preparations are heterogeneous and may contain non-vesicular co-isolates.
claims.rationale: MISEV2023 provides an expert-consensus framework for rigorous EV characterization and functional studies; it is not a product-specific regulatory approval standard.

claims.statement: Intranasal CNS delivery of EVs does not reliably translate across species: one macaque study found negligible brain uptake and no reliable CSF signal after intranasal administration of Expi293F-derived EVs.
claims.rationale: This directly limits extrapolation from rodent localization studies; differences in EV source, formulation, labeling, dosing, and administration remain possible explanations.

changes.summary: No material scientific change. Re-evaluated the pending candidate-definition decision and retained it for human review; the next action is to review the existing staged candidate-definition and quantitative biodistribution package before committing program resources.

evidence.title: Treatment of brain inflammatory diseases by delivering exosome encapsulated anti-inflammatory drugs from the nasal region to the brain
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: in mouse models, intranasal exosomes carrying curcumin or a STAT3 inhibitor were reported to reach brain microglia and improve model-specific inflammatory or tumor outcomes. These findings are preclinical and formulation-specific.

metadata.model_or_indication: mouse brain inflammation and glioma models

evidence.title: Intranasal MSC-derived A1-exosomes ease inflammation, and prevent abnormal neurogenesis and memory dysfunction after status epilepticus
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: after status epilepticus in young mice, intranasally administered human MSC-derived EVs were reported in the hippocampus and were associated with reduced neuronal loss and inflammation and preservation of neurogenesis and cognitive or memory outcomes versus vehicle.

evidence.title: Extracellular vesicles from immortalized mesenchymal stromal cells protect against neonatal hypoxic-ischemic brain injury
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: repeated intranasal EV administration after hypoxic-ischemic injury reduced brain tissue atrophy in neonatal mice; EVs from a clonal immortalized MSC line and primary MSCs showed comparable effects. The study frames source-cell consistency and scale as translational considerations.

evidence.title: Minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV2023): From basic to advanced approaches
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: the ISEV consensus identifies continuing challenges in EV nomenclature, separation from non-vesicular particles, characterization, functional studies, production reporting, and in-vivo evaluation; it recommends transparent, orthogonal characterization and appropriate controls.

evidence.title: Pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of extracellular vesicles administered intravenously and intranasally to Macaca nemestrina
evidence.excerpt: Curated summary: reporter-labeled Expi293F-derived EVs administered intranasally to macaques were not reliably detected above background in CSF, showed negligible brain uptake, and were strongly retained in nasal lavage. EV source, formulation, labeling, administration, and species may affect generalizability.

hypotheses.statement: An intranasal MSC-derived small-EV formulation with controlled identity, purity, dose, and potency attributes can achieve reproducible CNS exposure and a neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic signal in a cognition or aging model, but advancement should be gated on quantitative biodistribution and translation-oriented acceptance criteria.
hypotheses.rationale: Rodent CNS-injury studies support testing intranasal delivery and biological activity as enabling evidence rather than defining the intended indication; non-human-primate evidence makes delivery translation the principal uncertainty, and MISEV2023 supports tighter product characterization.
hypotheses.test_plan: Compare a characterized candidate formulation with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls; quantify intact-EV-associated exposure across CNS, nasal, pulmonary, and systemic compartments over time; pair exposure with a predefined neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic assay, then evaluate cognitive function in an aging-relevant model only if prospectively defined exposure, reproducibility, and safety criteria are met.

risks.title: Cross-species CNS delivery may fail
risks.description: Rodent CNS localization and efficacy may not translate to larger species or humans; nasal retention or anatomy may prevent adequate target-compartment exposure.
risks.mitigation: Establish quantitative, label-controlled biodistribution and pharmacokinetics with prospectively defined exposure criteria before indication-specific efficacy expansion.

risks.title: Product identity and potency may not be reproducible
risks.description: EV heterogeneity, co-isolates, source-cell variability, and process changes may alter composition, dose, stability, or biological activity.
risks.mitigation: Define the source-cell strategy, scalable purification process, orthogonal identity and purity panel, stability-indicating assays, and a mechanism-linked potency assay.

risks.title: Rodent efficacy may be model-specific
risks.description: Reported benefits span heterogeneous injury and inflammation models, EV sources, cargoes, schedules, and endpoints and therefore may not predict neuroregenerative or cognitive benefit for a defined SGL-001 product.
risks.mitigation: Select one lead indication and mechanism, predefine pharmacodynamic and efficacy endpoints, and replicate with the final candidate-like formulation in an adequately controlled study.

decisions.question: Should SGL-001 advance into broad cognition/neuroregeneration efficacy development now?
decisions.outcome: Do not advance into broad cognition/neuroregeneration efficacy development yet; propose a gated candidate-definition and quantitative biodistribution/pharmacology package for human approval.
decisions.rationale: Multiple rodent studies justify continued preclinical evaluation, but the non-human-primate result makes CNS delivery translation the largest unresolved risk, and EV identity, purity, dose, and potency must be controlled before efficacy can be attributed to a reproducible SGL-001 product.

Intranasal EV treatment was associated with improved inflammatory, histologic, or functional outcomes in several rodent CNS injury or disease models.

A clonal immortalized MSC source produced EVs with activity comparable to primary MSC-EVs in one neonatal mouse hypoxic-ischemic injury study, suggesting a testable route to reduce source heterogeneity during scale-up.

hypothesis.statement: An intranasal MSC-derived small-EV formulation with controlled identity, purity, dose, and potency attributes can achieve reproducible CNS exposure and a neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic signal in a cognition or aging model, but advancement should be gated on quantitative biodistribution and translation-oriented acceptance criteria.
hypothesis.whatChanged: No material scientific change. Re-evaluated the pending candidate-definition decision and retained it for human review; the next action is to review the existing staged candidate-definition and quantitative biodistribution package before committing program resources.

critique.strongestObjection: Authorization would be premature if interpreted as approval of a fixed product or efficacy program: the local evidence supports a gated learning package, not a final source-cell, purification process, dose, potency specification, exposure threshold, or clinical indication.
assumptionsChallenged: The evidence does not compare candidate-like SGL-001 formulations under a common manufacturing and analytical framework.
Rodent biological activity does not establish clinically relevant CNS exposure or human efficacy.
The macaque result materially weakens unqualified extrapolation of rodent intranasal delivery findings.
translationalConcerns: The hypothesis is plausible enough to test but remains highly sensitive to EV source, preparation purity, label artifacts, disease-model permeability, nasal retention, dose normalization, and cross-species anatomy. Rodent efficacy cannot establish that SGL-001 reaches a clinically relevant human CNS compartment or will benefit patients.
experimentalConfounders: Demonstrate that measured CNS signal represents intact candidate-associated EV exposure rather than free label, co-isolates, or secondary biological effects.
Define product identity, purity, dose units, stability, and a mechanism-relevant potency assay before interpreting efficacy reproducibility.
Use a staged translational plan because the macaque biodistribution result conflicts with assuming that rodent intranasal brain uptake will generalize to humans.
falsificationConditions: Compare a characterized candidate formulation with vehicle, free-label, and disrupted-EV controls; quantify intact-EV-associated exposure across CNS, nasal, pulmonary, and systemic compartments over time; pair exposure with a predefined neuroregeneration-relevant pharmacodynamic assay, then evaluate cognitive function in an aging-relevant model only if prospectively defined exposure, reproducibility, and safety criteria are met.

decision.rationale: Multiple rodent studies justify continued preclinical evaluation, but the non-human-primate result makes CNS delivery translation the largest unresolved risk, and EV identity, purity, dose, and potency must be controlled before efficacy can be attributed to a reproducible SGL-001 product.

cargo.rankingMethodology: Operator focus records the chosen development direction separately from evidence rank. Evidence rank reflects relevance and directness within the current local evidence only; it is not a validated efficacy score and does not override operator choice.

candidates.name: Native MSC-EV secretome cargo
candidates.source: MSC-derived small extracellular vesicles; final source-cell strategy not selected
candidates.mechanism: Multi-component paracrine signaling intended to support neuroregeneration-relevant and inflammation-modulating activity; active components remain undefined.
candidates.rationale: This is the operator-selected program focus because it preserves the multi-component EV thesis and has relevant rodent activity, while MISEV2023 highlights the characterization burden.
candidates.uncertainty: The active cargo components, potency mechanism, source-cell dependence, and relevance to cognition or aging are not established.

candidates.name: Curcumin-loaded EV benchmark
candidates.source: Exogenous curcumin loaded into an exosome preparation
candidates.mechanism: Delivery of an anti-inflammatory small-molecule payload using EVs as a carrier.
candidates.rationale: The current evidence is more cargo-specific than for the native secretome, making this an informative benchmark rather than the selected product focus.
candidates.uncertainty: The cited mouse models and loaded payload do not establish relevance to an unengineered SGL-001 product or human cognitive benefit.

candidates.name: STAT3-inhibitor-loaded EV benchmark
candidates.source: Exogenous STAT3 inhibitor loaded into an exosome preparation
candidates.mechanism: EV-mediated delivery of a pathway-directed inhibitor in a model-specific CNS context.
candidates.rationale: This is retained as a pathway-directed delivery benchmark, not as the current SGL-001 development focus.
candidates.uncertainty: Model-specific activity, payload safety, and relevance to cognition or aging remain unresolved.

pathways.name: Neuroinflammation modulation
pathways.description: Inflammation-modulating activity reported across local preclinical EV evidence; direction and causal cargo are product- and model-dependent.

pathways.name: Neurogenesis and neural plasticity
pathways.description: Preservation or modulation of neurogenesis and functional outcomes observed in rodent injury models, not established in aging or humans.

nextActions.action: Define the analytical comparison needed to distinguish native secretome activity from loaded-cargo benchmarks.
nextActions.objective: Make cargo strategy selection evidence-driven without displacing the operator-selected native EV focus.
nextActions.uncertainty: Whether native MSC-EV cargo provides reproducible neuroregeneration-relevant activity beyond cargo-loaded benchmarks.
successCriteria: A human-approved comparison plan links cargo measurements to a mechanism-relevant potency readout.

formulation.scoringMethodology: Each component is an uncalibrated ordinal assessment mapped as not_assessed=0, low=1, moderate=2, high=3. total_score is the inspectable component sum for directional comparison only; it is not a probability, validated product score, or approval criterion.

candidates.name: Characterized native MSC-EV intranasal candidate
candidates.activeCargoStrategy: Native secretome cargo; source and potency mechanism to be selected

score.methodology: Uncalibrated ordinal component sum; directional comparison only.

candidates.rationale: Matches the operator-selected program concept but remains insufficiently defined for manufacturing or clinical deployment.

candidates.name: Loaded-EV intranasal benchmark
candidates.modality: EV carrier with defined exogenous payload

score.methodology: Uncalibrated ordinal component sum; directional comparison only.

candidates.rationale: A more mechanistically inspectable benchmark scores directionally above the native focus despite not being the chosen product thesis.
tradeoffs: Does not establish cognition or aging relevance

candidates.name: Uncharacterized conditioned-medium nasal product

score.methodology: Uncalibrated ordinal component sum; directional comparison only.

candidates.rationale: The broad secretome may be easier to produce but prevents clear attribution of identity, dose, and potency.
candidates.exclusionReason: Excluded from the current product definition because the local evidence does not support adequate identity, purity, or potency control.

excipients.name: Isotonic aqueous vehicle, composition TBD
excipients.risk: Vehicle composition may alter EV integrity, nasal retention, tolerability, and measured biodistribution.

excipients.name: EV-compatible stabilizer, not yet selected
excipients.risk: No local evidence currently supports a specific stabilizer or concentration for intranasal SGL-001.

nextActions.uncertainty: Whether a reproducible candidate-like formulation can support interpretable biodistribution and pharmacology.

jurisdictions.disclaimer: Planning state only, not legal advice. Verdicts distinguish legal pathway evidence from enforcement observations and require current regulator verification and qualified local counsel before action.

jurisdictions.productClassification: FDA states that exosome products intended to treat disease are generally regulated as drugs and biological products and require premarket review and approval.
jurisdictions.privateClinicPath: No legitimate routine private-clinic deployment path is identified for an unapproved SGL-001 therapeutic. Human administration would require an applicable authorized clinical investigation or approved product pathway.
jurisdictions.conciseRationale: FDA sources support an investigational or approved-product pathway, not routine deployment of an unapproved therapeutic exosome product in private clinics.
